questions.text: Explain the differences between the Shvetambara and Digambara sects.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the differences between the Shvetambara and Digambara sects. (Difficult)

answer.value:
Differences between the Shwetambara and Digambara sects (printed as a comparison table):
Dress: Shwetambara - 'Shweta' means white; the monks of this sect wear white clothes. Digambara - 'Dig' means direction; the directions themselves are their clothing; the monks remain completely Digambara (without clothes/nude).
Women's liberation (Moksha): Shwetambara - women can also attain Moksha in this very birth. Digambara - women cannot attain Moksha directly; they must be born as men in the next birth and only then can they attain Moksha.
Marriage of Mahavira: Shwetambara - Vardhamana Mahavira was married to Yashoda and had a daughter named 'Priyadarshana'. Digambara - Mahavira never married and remained a celibate throughout his life.
Food consumption: Shwetambara - even after attaining Kevala Jnana (omniscience), a living enlightened person still requires food. Digambara - those who have attained Kevala Jnana (Arahants) have neither hunger nor thirst; therefore they do not require food.
